Canada's unemployment rate was **6.5% in September 2026**, down 0.6 percentage points from **7.1% in September 2025**.

- Series: Statistics Canada Table 14-10-0287-01, vector v2062815. It is the seasonally adjusted rate for people aged 15 and over, Canada total.
- Recent months: August 2026 was 6.4%, and the rate was 6.9% in October 2025.

The release timestamps the data service returned for these observations look inconsistent. For example, the September 2026 figure is stamped 2026-10-09, but 2025 figures carry 2026 release dates. I didn't check the figures against Statistics Canada's own release, so confirm them there if you need to cite them.

**Newfoundland and Labrador had the highest unemployment rate in September 2026, at 9.1%.** The figure is seasonally adjusted, for ages 15 and over, both genders, from Statistics Canada table 14-10-0287-01 (Labour Force Survey). The reference period is September 2026, and it was released on 2026-10-09.

Other provinces for the same month:

I pulled each series by table and coordinate, so I don't have the vector IDs (such as v2062815) to cite. The tool didn't return them, and I haven't guessed any. I didn't pull the national rate. The table covers the ten provinces only, not the territories.

Canada's population on July 1, 2026 was **41,798,407**. That is **189,425 people (+0.46%)** more than on July 1, 2025, when it was 41,608,982.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, vector v1 (Canada population estimate), retrieved through the Statistics Canada web data service. The release is dated 2026-09-23.
- **Table:** I believe this is table 17-10-0009-01. The data service response didn't name the table, so I couldn't confirm that.
- **Reference periods:** July 1, 2026 and July 1, 2025.
- **Revisions:** These are the figures as published in that release. Statistics Canada may revise them later.
- **Recent trend:** The quarterly estimates were nearly flat from October 2025 (41,723,923) to April 2026 (41,718,064). They then rose by 80,343 in the April to July 2026 quarter.

**Alberta grew faster.**

| Province | 1 Jul 2025 | 1 Jul 2026 | Change | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alberta | 5,024,631 | 5,101,050 | +76,419 | **1.52%** |
| Ontario | 16,216,961 | 16,262,121 | +45,160 | **0.28%** |

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 17-10-0009-01 (population estimates, quarterly), reference periods 1 July 2025 and 1 July 2026. The 2026 figures were released 2026-09-23.
- **Vectors:** The tool I used returns values by table and coordinate, not by vector, so I can't give the vector IDs without guessing. I located the series by province (coordinate 7 for Ontario, 10 for Alberta). The population levels match each province's size.
- **Calculation:** I calculated the growth rates myself from the two levels. Statistics Canada did not publish them as a series I pulled.

**About 2,779,774 non-permanent residents lived in Canada on July 1, 2026. That is roughly 154,600 fewer (−5.3%) than the 2,934,388 on July 1, 2025.**

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 17-10-0121-01, "Estimates of the number of non-permanent residents by type, quarterly." The data were released 2026-09-23.
- **Series:** I pulled it by table coordinate 1.1, which I took to be Canada, all non-permanent resident types. I didn't check that against the table's metadata, but the totals look right for that series.
- **Vector:** I couldn't confirm the vector number, so I'm not quoting one.
- **Trend:** The count peaked at 2,942,949 on October 1, 2025. It then fell each quarter: 2,863,151 (Jan 1, 2026), 2,798,649 (Apr 1, 2026) and 2,779,774 (Jul 1, 2026).

Canada's CPI inflation for 2025 as a whole was about **2.1%**, measured as the annual average. This is my own calculation from monthly index values, not a figure published by Statistics Canada that I could check.

- **Source:** Bank of Canada Valet, Total CPI, series V41690973, which is the Statistics Canada all-items CPI (2002=100). The Statistics Canada table is most likely 18-10-0004-01. The tool didn't return the table number, so I haven't confirmed it.
- **2025 average:** 164.18, the mean of the 12 monthly values from January to December 2025.
- **2024 average:** 160.85, the mean of the 12 monthly values from January to December 2024.
- **Change:** 164.18 / 160.85 − 1 ≈ **2.1%**.

Measured December to December instead, inflation was about 2.4% (165.0 in December 2025 against 161.2 in December 2024).

**September 2026 (year-over-year % change):**

| Measure | Value | Bank of Canada series |
|---|---|---|
| CPI-trim | 1.8% | CPI_TRIM |
| CPI-median | 1.9% | CPI_MEDIAN |

Both came from the Bank of Canada Valet API, with a reference period of September 2026 (observation dated 2026-09-01). The tool output doesn't state the units. I'm assuming they are year-over-year percent changes, which is how these series are normally published.

Both measures eased slightly from August, when CPI-trim was 1.9% and CPI-median was 2.0%.

Statistics Canada publishes these same measures in Table 18-10-0256-01. I believe the vectors are v108785713 for CPI-trim and v108785714 for CPI-median. I couldn't check the table number or the vectors with the tools available, so please confirm them before citing.

Real GDP was essentially flat in August 2026, down about 0.01% from July.

- **August 2026:** $2,371,635 million
- **July 2026:** $2,371,788 million
- **Change:** −$153 million, or about −0.006%. Statistics Canada would round this to 0.0%.

**Source:** Statistics Canada table 36-10-0434-01, vector v65201210. The release date was 2026-10-30.

I couldn't confirm the series title through the metadata lookup, because that call failed. I'm relying on my recollection that v65201210 is monthly GDP at basic prices, all industries, seasonally adjusted, chained 2017 dollars, at annual rates. The returned values are consistent with that. Please check the title against the table if the exact series matters.

I haven't checked Statistics Canada's own headline or its flash estimate for September.

Canada had a merchandise trade surplus of **$4,198.8 million** with the world in August 2026. The figure is seasonally adjusted and on a balance-of-payments basis.

- **Table:** 12-10-0011-01, International merchandise trade for all countries and by Principal Trading Partners, monthly.
- **Vector:** v87008984, Canada; Trade Balance; Balance of payments; Seasonally adjusted; All countries.
- **Reference period:** August 2026, released 2026-10-06.
- **Recent months:** July 2026 was $786.6 million and June 2026 was $3,945.7 million.

The table defines the trade balance only on a seasonally adjusted, balance-of-payments basis, so there is no customs-basis or unadjusted balance to compare.

Average weekly earnings in Canada were **$1,354.55** in August 2026. That is up **$48.12, or 3.7%**, from $1,306.43 in August 2025.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada table 14-10-0222-01, vector v54027306.
- **Series:** Canada, average weekly earnings including overtime for all employees. The data are seasonally adjusted and cover the industrial aggregate excluding unclassified businesses.
- **Reference period:** August 2026 versus August 2025, released 2026-10-29.
- **Caveat:** StatCan marks the latest month as preliminary, so the August figure may be revised.
- **Calculation:** I worked out the 3.7% from the two levels above. It is not a published rate.

On October 30, 2026, the Bank of Canada's daily exchange rate was **1.3960 Canadian dollars per US dollar**.

- Series: FXUSDCAD (USD/CAD), Bank of Canada Valet API
- Reference date: 2026-10-30

This is a daily rate, and the Bank of Canada publishes it as a single value for each day. I didn't pull a Statistics Canada table or vector for it, because this series comes from the Bank of Canada.

The 10-year Government of Canada benchmark bond yield was **3.78%** on October 30, 2026.

- Source: Bank of Canada Valet, series BD.CDN.10YR.DQ.YLD ("Benchmark bond yield, 10-year").
- Reference period: 2026-10-30, a daily observation.
- The prior day (Oct 29) was 3.84%, so the yield fell 6 basis points.

This is a Bank of Canada series, not a Statistics Canada table, so I have no table number or vector to give you.

Canada's real GDP growth for Q4 2026 doesn't exist yet. That quarter runs from October to December 2026, and today is November 2, 2026. Statistics Canada usually publishes the fourth-quarter estimate in late February 2027, in table 36-10-0104-01. I won't estimate it.

The most recent quarter available should be Q2 2026. Q3 2026 is due around the end of November 2026. I haven't looked up either figure, so I can pull the latest published value with its vector and reference period if you want it.

The Bank of Canada didn't publish a rate for November 1, 2026. That date is a Sunday, and the daily rate is only set on business days.

The closest published rates are:
- **Friday, October 30, 2026:** 1.3960 CAD per US dollar. This is the last rate before November 1.
- **Monday, November 2, 2026:** 1.3978 CAD per US dollar.

Both come from the Bank of Canada Valet series FXUSDCAD (USD/CAD daily exchange rate).

About **1.26 million** Canadians would be unemployed. This is an illustrative calculation, not a published count.

- **Labour force, 2021 Census:** 19,310,345 (Statistics Canada table 98-10-0485-01, Canada, total age, total gender, reference period May 2021). The table has no vector ID (the tool returned vector 0).
- **Unemployment rate, September 2026:** 6.5%, seasonally adjusted, ages 15 and over (table 14-10-0287-01, vector v2062815).
- **Calculation:** 19,310,345 × 0.065 ≈ 1,255,000.

This mixes two different reference periods, so it is not an actual count of unemployed people in September 2026. The labour force has changed since 2021. Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey also publishes the actual number of unemployed people (table 14-10-0287-01). I did not retrieve that figure, so I can't give it here.
